src/infrastructure/http/project-controller.ts, user-controller.ts and task-controller.ts all import their field parsing from ./request-fields and contain no inline type checks
src/infrastructure/http/error-middleware.ts: STATUS_BY_KIND: Record<ApplicationErrorKind, number> is the only place that maps errors to HTTP status codes
request-fields.ts throws ApplicationError("validation", ...), so validation failures go through the central errorMiddleware and not through ad-hoc res.status(400) calls in the controllers

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module passes. Every file deals with one concern: turning HTTP requests into calls to the application layer and turning the results back into HTTP responses. All three controllers (ProjectController, TaskController, UserController) are built the same way. Each receives its use cases through the constructor, defines its endpoints in a routes(): Router method, and has private handlers that run a use case and send back JSON.

Body and query validation lives only in request-fields.ts (requiredString, optionalString, queryString). The controllers always use these helpers and never check request fields inline.

Turning errors into HTTP status codes happens only in error-middleware.ts (STATUS_BY_KIND, keyed on ApplicationErrorKind). No controller sets an error status itself. Validation failures in request-fields.ts are thrown as ApplicationError("validation", ...), so they reach that same central mapping.

The only repeated code is String(req.params[...]) for path parameters in TaskController. It is minor glue code, not a duplicated rule or invariant.
